licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cleanly partition the distribution by grouping items around the core disciplinary themes present across states: deceptive acts in obtaining or using a license (Fraud or Misrepresentation), substandard or unsafe work quality (Incompetence or Negligence), criminal history (Criminal Conviction), violations of statutes, codes, or board rules (Regulatory or Code Violation), unlicensed practice or license lending/transfer (License Misuse or Unlicensed Practice), abandonment, fund diversion, non-payment, and contract failures (Contract or Financial Misconduct), procedural failures such as missing records, insurance, permits, CE, or board orders (Administrative Non-Compliance), drug or alcohol impairment affecting fitness (Substance Abuse or Fitness), and sanctions imposed by another jurisdiction (Out-of-State Discipline).

profession_specific.license_tiers.rationale: The data clusters naturally around the classic trade ladder (apprentice → journeyman → master), the business-entity contractor license, a large group of scope-restricted or trade-specific licenses (residential wireman, sign, fire alarm, low voltage, renewable energy, etc.), supervisory/administrator credentials that sit above journeyman but outside the master path, and a small residual group covering inspectors and unclassified roles.

profession_specific.scope_exclusions.rationale: These nine buckets cleanly separate the dominant clusters in the data: regulated utility infrastructure, telecom/low-voltage/signal systems, owner-occupant self-help, employer in-plant maintenance, adjacent licensed trades (HVAC, elevators, alarms, plumbing), agricultural settings, mobile/vehicle equipment, government-entity carve-outs, and the residual of trivial plug-in/minor repairs—together covering virtually every row without forcing unrelated items into a catch-all.
